blocks.x: A tuning factory, not a notebook: decontaminated datasets, multi-task eval gates that block silent regressions, distillation that keeps quality while cutting serving cost, and canary rollout with a rehearsed rollback path.
Fine-tuning as a data-engineering program — the GPU is the smallest part
blocks.sub: Dataset quality, leakage discipline and eval matrices decide the outcome

blocks.x: Fine-tuning is a data engineering program that occasionally involves a GPU. The wins come from dataset construction — decontamination, label consistency, hard-negative mining — and the losses come from skipping the eval design and discovering regressions in front of users.

The operational half matters more each quarter: drift watch on live traffic, promotion gates with automatic rollback, distillation pipelines that keep the cheap model close to the expensive one. Tuned models are liabilities unless they are versioned, monitored and reversible.
Below: the failure modes that produce quietly bad models, the factory architecture that prevents them, and the gates a tuned model clears before it serves a real user.
Contamination to silent regressions — how tuning goes quietly bad
blocks.sub: Contamination, off-task regressions, unsigned lineage, no canary

blocks.x: None of these failures announce themselves in the demo — they surface weeks later in production, which is why each countermeasure is structural rather than procedural.

widgets.title: Model operations cycle — click stages for the contract

stages.name: Monitor
stages.detail: Input and output distributions tracked per feature; drift alarms carry the evidence window so retraining decisions cite data, not vibes.

stages.name: Triage
stages.detail: Regression triage separates model drift from upstream changes (retrieval index, prompt change, product edit) — the harness replays golden cases to attribute.

stages.name: Re-tune
stages.detail: Corrections from production join the curated set with provenance; the training mix rebalances; the new candidate trains on spot capacity.

stages.name: Gate
stages.detail: Task quality, capability retention, safety — all three must clear. A candidate that wins the task and loses retention is rejected by arithmetic.

stages.name: Promote
stages.detail: Shadow scoring against live traffic, canary at 5%, promotion with rollback pinned — the harness result travels with the model version.

widgets.note: The treadmill is scheduled work: drift alarms arrive, the cycle runs, the harness decides — nobody hand-rolls a fine-tune in a crisis.

Decontamination is the first gate
blocks.sub: Dataset engineering as the program — leakage tests, task matrices and the promotion path

blocks.x: Tuned models fail quietly through contamination: eval questions leaking into training data make the golden set flatter than reality, and the regression appears only in production phrasing. The factory therefore runs decontamination as a hard gate — n-gram and embedding-similarity scans against every eval split, with provenance recorded per document — before any GPU hour is spent. The multi-task eval matrix then protects against the classic LoRA failure: gains on the target task that quietly degrade general capability, so every candidate runs the full matrix and regression on any off-task domain blocks promotion.

Method selection is budget-matched engineering, not fashion: LoRA for narrow style/format shifts, full tuning when behavior must move and data supports it, distillation when serving cost dominates. The registry carries signed dataset lineage — every training document traceable to its source and license class — and the promotion path ends in a canary ring before estate-wide serving, because the last mile of a tune is operational, not academic.

How do you prevent training-data contamination?

Decontamination is the first gate: datasets are deduplicated against the eval suite and screened for benchmark leakage before a run starts. A tune that cannot prove a clean dataset does not reach the eval gates.
What stops a tune from quietly regressing on tasks we did not test?

The eval suite is multi-task and versioned — a candidate must hold the floor on every task family, not just average well. Regressions below the floor block promotion, and the console shows the per-task deltas.
Is fine-tuning always better than prompting a frontier model?

No — the chart is the argument: we size the smallest model whose quality holds the floor for the task, and distillation happens only where the eval deltas justify it. The factory prices quality against serving cost per task.
Can our team run the factory after handover?
Yes — dataset lineage, eval harness, canary cadence and the promotion gates are documented and owned by your team at handover; we support the first two promotion cycles.
How do you handle regulated data in training sets?

The data path inherits the platform’s controls: consent and retention are checked at dataset admission, lineage runs from source to canary, and the governance overlay names what an examiner can reconstruct.
